newsitem.title: UK: IPE May Brent closes below eight month low.
newsitem.headline: IPE May Brent closes below eight month low.

text.p: Late technically-led selling on the May IPE Brent saw the contract break and close below two main support levels as traders liquidated their positions in relatively thin volumes, brokers said.
May Brent ended the day down some 60 cents at $18.50 a barrel, a new eight month low, well below the triple bottom of $18.67 from July 29, 1996.
On a continuation basis the next support level comes in just four cents below the close at $18.46, the low from June 27, followed by the June 26 low of $18.16 a barrel.
Brokers said a fundamentally weak market was putting pressure on the outright price.
"There is too much crude around so the price wants to come down. It looks like we could head lower again tomorrow. It's extremely bearish," one said.

May WTI which held above support at $19.85 a barrel until after the IPE closed, then broke down to a low of $19.65. By 1943 GMT the contract had regained some ground to trade down 55 cents on the day at $19.73 a barrel.
April gas oil, which closed earlier unchanged at $165.50 a tonne, was called to open down some $2-$2.50 a tonne on the basis of the Brent close and weakness on the NYMEX heating oil.
